## Purpose

Compute and persist an explainable module proposal without running pytest.

## When a playbook uses it

An explicit validation step attached to a live worker claim. The smart runner consumes the proposal; requesting a selection alone verifies no tests.

## How it works internally

The handler checks the feature flags and mode, fences the held claim, derives the workspace from the authenticated session, and calls `SelectionService.select`. Only a local operator supplies a workspace and receives full-suite authorization. See [`test_selection_commands.py`](../../../src/commands/test_selection_commands.py) and [`service.py`](../../../src/test_selection/service.py).

## Side effects and persistence

Creates one immutable `test_selections` row per request, even for cached recommendations, and emits `test_selection.recorded.v1`. Records retain digests, reason codes, argument arrays and pending obligations; no raw diff or provider key is returned.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`disabled`, `enforce_not_enabled`, `invalid_mode` and `narrowing_flags` reject unsupported requests. `stale_claim` requires a current claim epoch; `spoofed_workspace` means a worker supplied a workspace. `workspace_required` / `workspace_invalid` diagnose local path errors. `out_of_scope` means no eligible held task. A `full_required` success is a planning result, not permission for a worker to run the whole suite.

## Example step

Command-step payload (promotion/revocation examples require a local operator context):

```json
{"command": "test_select", "args": {"claim_epoch": 7, "mode": "shadow", "targets": ["tests/test_selection_commands.py"], "jev": false}}
```
